en: May that certain auspicious form named Gaṇeśa bestow prosperity upon me—she who, though always appearing in the form of a child, is the destroyer of the mountain of obstacles; who, though possessing the face of a great elephant, is honored as the five-faced one; and who is sought after by Brahmā, Indra, and the other gods.

I do not know sound, nor do I know meaning; I do not know verse, nor do I know prose. Yet the one Consciousness shines within my heart, O Six-faced One, and it is a marvel that words issue forth from my mouth! 2.

I worship the protector of the world, who is mounted upon a peacock, hidden within the Great Sayings (Mahāvākya), possessing a body that captivates the mind, the great abode of consciousness, the god of the gods among the Brahmins, the essence of the great Vedas, and the child of Mahādeva. ||3||

I praise that pure son of Parāśakti who dwells on the shore of the ocean, manifesting this thought: "When human beings come into my presence, they have at that very moment reached the further shore of the ocean of existence. 4.

"Just as the lofty waves of the ocean dissolve away, so too shall calamities vanish for those who serve Me"—showing this very lesson through the rows of his waves, I shall always meditate upon that Guha within the lotus of my heart. (5)

"Those men who have ascended the mountain, the abode of Manmatha, now shine as they have ascended the mountain [of fragrance]. May that six-faced god, who spoke thus while ascending the Mountain of Fragrance (Gandhamādana), be forever for my delight. 6.

We take refuge in that Guha, who dwells in a cave on the fragrant mountain named Sugandha—favored by the Lord of Sages, situated on the shore of the great ocean, and free from the thieves of great evil—who shines with his own radiance and removes the suffering of living beings. (7)

I shall always meditate upon Kārttikeya, the lord of the gods, who resides in a palace of shining gold that fulfills the desires of men, seated upon a couch of rubies covered with a multitude of beautiful cloths, and possessing a radiance equal to a thousand rising suns. (8)

O Skanda, may my mind-bee, scorched by the afflictions of worldly existence, ever delight in your lotus-feet, which resound with the cry of swans, are beautiful, intensely crimson, and filled with the nectar of captivating loveliness. (9)
O Skanda, I meditate upon your radiant waist, shining with divine garments of golden luster, beautified by a girdle of tinkling bells, and illuminated by a gleaming golden band. 10.

O Destroyer of Tāraka, I bow to your chest, which is ever full of passion for the protection of your own devotees, and which is stained with saffron paste from embracing the full, high breasts of the mountain-dwelling maidens. 11.

I ever take refuge in your fierce staff-like arms, which have meted out punishment according to the law, which uphold the cosmic egg through their own play, which have cast aside the trunks of rival elephants, which are like the staff of Death to your enemies, which have slain the hosts of Indra’s foes, and which are ever intent on protecting the world. (12)

O Skanda, if there were always six autumnal moons rising together and remaining stationed on all sides, their full discs forever free from blemish, only then could I speak of a likeness between them and your faces.

O Son of the Lord of the Earth, whose lips flow with nectar, I behold Your six lotus-like faces, radiant with swarms of bees in the form of flickering side-glances, together with quivering gentle smiles. 14.

"Come here, my child"—if even a single slight sidelong glance were cast upon me by Your twelve eyes, which are wide, reaching to the tips of Your ears, and constantly overflowing with compassion, O You whose nature is mercy, what loss indeed could there be? (15)

O Lord of the World, salutations to those heads of yours, radiant with crowns, which bear the burden of the universe and from which the Lord joyfully smells—repeating the mantra "May you live" six times—as they emerge from the limbs of his daughter. 16.

May the son of Purāri stand before me—he who is beautiful with shimmering jeweled armlets and necklaces, whose cheeks are radiant with the splendor of swinging earrings, who wears yellow garments upon his waist and holds a lovely spear in his hand. 17.
Stretching out his hands, he calls with reverence to Śaṅkara from his mother’s lap; I worship that child-form who, leaping up, takes refuge in his father as his body is embraced by Hara. 18.

O son of Kumāreśa, Guha, Skanda, Generalissimo, wielder of the spear, mounted upon a peacock; O beloved of the daughter of Pulinda, remover of the distress of devotees, Lord, slayer of Tāraka, protect me always! 19.

When my senses have become tranquil, consciousness has vanished, my body is motionless, my mouth is foaming with phlegm, and my limbs tremble with fear, and I am about to depart—then, O Guha, you who are compassionate, quickly come before me, for I am now without a protector. (20)

While the fierce messengers of Kṛtānta, out of anger, threaten me with cries of "Burn! Cut! Break!", do you, bearing a spear in hand, quickly come before me, riding a peacock and saying, "Do not fear! (21)

Having prostrated repeatedly at Your feet and fallen down, O Lord, I entreat You many times after having propitiated You; yet, O Ocean of Mercy, I am not able to speak [further] then—for at the time of the end of one's task, not even the slightest neglect should be shown.

O Lord, you have slain Tāraka, the consumer of a thousand eggs, who bore the name Śūra, as well as the Daitya Siṃhavaktra; yet you do not destroy this single affliction of my mind that dwells within my heart—what shall I do, and where shall I go? (23)

I am always overwhelmed by the burden of suffering; O Friend of the Wretched, I beg no one other than you. O Son of Umā, quickly destroy my mental anguish, which obstructs devotion to you and is constantly attended by affliction. 24.

O Destroyer of Tāraka, upon seeing the ash from your foot, great diseases such as epilepsy, leprosy, consumption, hemorrhoids, urinary disorders, fever, insanity, and abdominal tumors, as well as all piśācas, flee in an instant. (25)
May his form be in my sight, his fame in my hearing, and his pure conduct always in my mouth; may his deed be in my hand, his body in my servant, and all my dispositions be absorbed in Guha. (26)

Deities exist everywhere, bestowing desired objects upon sages as well as upon men who possess devotion; yet, for the sake of granting one's own self-interest even to the lowest-born among men, I know no other deity than Guha—I truly know no other. 27.

O Kumāra, may all those who belong to my household—whether wife, sons, circle of kinsmen, cattle, men, or women—who sacrifice to you, bow before you, praise you, and remember you, become [your devotees]. (28)

May the deer, birds, gadflies, and whatever wicked things, as well as the diseases that afflict my body, perish far away, shattered by the sharp points of your power—O you who crushed the Krauñca mountain! (29)

O Lord of the celestial army, do not mother and father ever tolerate the offense of their own son? I am but a mere child, while you are the father of the world; therefore, O Great Lord, forgive me for every transgression. (30)

Salutations to you, the peacock; salutations also to you, the spear; salutations to you, O goat; salutations to the cock. Salutations to the ocean and to the land of Sindhu; again, salutations to you who are the very form of Skanda—may there be salutations to you.

Victory to you, O son of the Lord of Liberators! You who possess a splendor that conquers the earth, you whose fame is unfailing, you whose form is bliss; victory to you, O ocean of joy, victory to you, the friend of all; may you ever be victorious!

The man who, having bowed deeply to Guha, recites this hymn composed in the *bhujaṅgaprayāta* meter with devotion, shall obtain sons, a wife, wealth, and long life; in the end, he attains union with Skanda.
Thus ends the *Śrīsubrahmaṇyabhujaṅga* composed by the venerable Śrī Śaṅkarabhagavat.
